title: Why rep counting requires confirmation
text: Instantaneous single-frame joint angles are noisy, so a rep counter should require the target angle to be held for at least two consecutive frames before switching state. This two-tick confirmation prevents a flicker between standing and bottom positions from producing a phantom rep, especially when the pose estimator briefly loses a joint.

title: Camera view for squat analysis
text: A front-view camera is well suited for detecting dynamic knee valgus and hip drop during a squat, while a side-view camera is required to measure knee-over-toe translation and torso lean. If only one camera is available, a 45-degree oblique view compromises between the two.

title: Warm-up before rehabilitation exercise
text: A five-minute low-intensity warm-up (marching in place, gentle cycling, or air squats to a comfortable depth) raises tissue temperature and improves range of motion before loaded rehabilitation work. Static stretching before strength training is generally avoided because it briefly reduces force production.

title: Pain during exercise
text: Mild discomfort during rehabilitation exercise is usually acceptable, but sharp pain, giving-way, or swelling that persists more than two hours after a session are signs the load or range should be reduced. The patient should be advised to contact their physiotherapist rather than push through pain.
